skills.name: Decolonisation case study: the Gold Coast becomes Ghana

note.text: The Gold Coast’s route to independence combined African political mobilisation, elections and negotiation under changing British rule. Kwame Nkrumah’s Convention People’s Party pressed for self-government and gained electoral strength. Constitutional changes expanded African responsibility before sovereignty was transferred. Internal self-government did not yet remove every power reserved to the colonial governor. Ghana became independent on 6 March 1957. This was a political process with disagreements, not a gift requiring no African action or a guarantee of all future outcomes.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to connect nationalist organisation, constitutional change and independence without erasing African agency. Builds on: Form Four nationalism and postwar international change. Leads to: comparison with Nigeria and French West Africa.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: The Gold Coast’s route to independence combined African political mobilisation, elections and negotiation under changing British rule. Kwame Nkrumah’s Convention People’s Party pressed for self-government and gained electoral strength. Constitutional changes expanded African responsibility before sovereignty was transferred. Internal self-government did not yet remove every power reserved to the colonial governor. Ghana became independent on {6} March {1957}. This was a political process with disagreements, not a gift requiring no African action or a guarantee of all future outcomes.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: The CPP’s electoral success in {1951} contributed to Nkrumah’s release from imprisonment and entry into government. He became prime minister in {1952}; the {1954} constitution widened internal self-government while some powers remained reserved. Independence in {1957} changed sovereign status. An official British debate provides evidence of constitutional proposals and its speakers’ viewpoints; it does not represent every Ghanaian voice.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

cards.idea: Connect a specific action or event to the historical feature it illustrates.

The {1954} constitution increased internal self-government while reserved powers remained.
A British parliamentary debate records proposals and disagreement, not all Ghanaian opinion.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Ghanaian independence occurred without African political organisation. Correction: African parties and mobilisation were central to the process.
Internal self-government meant every colonial power had already disappeared. Correction: Reserved authority distinguished autonomy from full sovereignty.
Ghana became independent only after Nigeria in {1960}. Correction: Ghana’s independence preceded Nigeria’s.
A speech by one official proves unanimous popular consent. Correction: Other voices and evidence are needed to assess wider opinion.
